title: Design and Implementation of a High-Frequency Charge-Pump PFC Resonant Converter for a USB-C Power Supply

takeaway.text: A compact USB-C supply must regulate power as devices and their demands change.

speaker_notes: This thesis covers the design and implementation of a USB-C power supply using a high-frequency charge-pump power-factor-correction resonant converter. The aim is a compact supply for a device whose demand can change during operation. The design target is 100 watts continuous, with a 65-watt continuous minimum. A device may be absent at startup, connected later, or removed while energy remains in the converter. The supply therefore needs to control transferred power across changing load conditions.
transition: The range of USB-C adapters illustrates the different power and voltage demands behind this design.
